title: H2O2 Content Measurement in Wild Jujube Seedlings
author: Mingxin Guo
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.jqjcmun

steps.title: Grow seedlings to six-leaf stage
steps.instruction: Cultivate wild jujube seedlings in Kimura’s culture solution B until they reach the six‑leaf stage.

steps.title: Alkaline treatment of root samples
steps.instruction: Take 0.5 g of fresh root from each seedling and expose it to an alkaline solution adjusted to pH 9.5 for 0, 3, or 5 days, depending on the experimental group.

steps.title: Incubate roots in TTC solution
steps.instruction: After the alkaline treatment, incubate the 0.5 g root sample in 10 mL of triphenyl tetrazolium chloride (TTC) solution (0.04 % TTC in pH 7.0 phosphate buffer) for 1 hour at 37 °C.

steps.title: Add H2SO4 and extract product
steps.instruction: Add 2 mL of 1 M H₂SO₄ to the incubated sample, then extract the resulting red TTC‑forbidden product from the root tissue using ethyl acetate.

substeps.instruction: Add 2 mL 1 M H₂SO₄ to the tube.
Extract the red product with ethyl acetate.

steps.title: Measure absorbance at 485 nm
steps.instruction: Determine the absorbance of the ethyl‑acetate extract with a spectrophotometer set to 485 nm.

steps.title: Calculate relative activity
steps.instruction: Express the H₂O₂‑related activity of each root sample as a percentage of the control (set to 100 %).
